person: Samira Okoye is a 32-year-old marketing project coordinator, married six weeks ago and expecting in the autumn. Her mother, Ngozi, died on 14 February 2026, and Samira is the court-appointed personal representative of the estate. Her father, 84, lives with her and she pays his two part-time caregivers. She is organised and good with apps but has never dealt with government paperwork, and her new married name appears only on the marriage certificate, so the court papers and her mother's accounts all carry her maiden name. Her mother's mail is forwarded to her Gmail, and she has just realised that the nine-month disclaimer window closes in three weeks. She wants an order of steps, to know which ones carry a penalty if late, and to be told when she needs an accountant.
stated_up_front: Okay, I made a list for my mom's estate and I'm a little panicked because someone said there's a nine-month deadline on something. Can you go through her mail and accounts with me and tell me what order to do things in and what's actually urgent?

facts.about: Date of death and disclaimer window
facts.truth: Her mother, Ngozi Okoye, died 14 February 2026. Samira counts nine months from then, so the disclaimer deadline is around 14 November 2026.
The county probate court appointed her personal representative on 2 April 2026, and the letters are in her maiden name, Samira Okoye.
She married on 5 September 2026 and uses her husband's surname, Adeyemi, but only the marriage certificate shows it. Nothing else has been updated.
She opened an estate checking account at Chase. It holds about $23,400, mostly from the mother's closed savings account.

The mother had a traditional IRA at Fidelity worth about $61,000. Samira is the named beneficiary and her brother Tobenna is the contingent. She has not taken any distribution and is unsure whether to keep it or disclaim it.
Mutual of Omaha drafted a $212 premium from the mother's old checking account in March, after her death. Samira wants it refunded.
A collection agency wrote about a $4,180 credit card balance and asked Samira to pay it with her own card. She has not responded.
A $1,946 bill from St. Mary's Hospital arrived. She thinks the Medigap plan already paid it, but she has not checked the EOB.
A letter says the mother was overpaid $1,318 for February. Samira thinks the bank already sent that money back.
A search of the state unclaimed property site shows $640 under 'Ngozi Okoye', but there is also another Ngozi Okoye in a different city.
He is 84 and lives with her. He is not the executor and has asked her not to bother him with the paperwork.
Her husband Daniel and her father both assume she has everything handled. She hasn't hired a lawyer or accountant, and her mother's old tax returns are in a Drive folder.

unknowns: Whether the IRA disclaimer is still available, or whether anything she has already done counts as accepting it
What the creditor claim deadline is, and whether the collector's claim would be late
Whether the mother owed any final income tax to the IRS
Whether the $640 unclaimed property record belongs to her mother
Whether the mother had any group life policy through her old employer
